paragraphs: As of Wednesday, October 7, before the U.S. open, the Nasdaq enters the session at another record but with a less comfortable cross-asset backdrop than Tuesday's close. The Nasdaq Composite gained 0.45% Tuesday to 27,599.79, while the S&P 500 rose 0.58%; six of the Magnificent Seven advanced and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained ground. The AI complex also received fresh confirmation from Marvell's stronger long-range data-center outlook and AMD's plan to materially increase chip supply in 2027. Importantly, Tuesday's rally was helped by easing Treasury yields and steadier crude, while the market-implied probability of another Fed hike in October fell to about 19%. I did not use a Nasdaq-100 futures quote because I could not verify one published before the 06:00 Turkey-time cutoff.

The overnight picture is more balanced. By 05:40 Turkey time, the U.S. 10-year yield had rebounded to around 5.30%, Brent was near $101.65 and WTI near $90.38 as a developing Gulf of Mexico storm threatened U.S. energy infrastructure and Saudi-Houthi tensions intensified. That partially reverses Tuesday's favorable rates-and-oil impulse. Nasdaq breadth also deserves caution despite the record: Tuesday's Nasdaq advancers only narrowly exceeded decliners, 2,394 to 2,378, and the exchange recorded 61 new highs versus 182 new lows. The setup therefore remains supported by strong AI/semiconductor momentum, but today's test is whether that leadership can absorb renewed oil and long-yield pressure ahead of the Fed minutes.

catalysts.title: FOMC minutes — 2:00 ET / 21:00 Istanbul
catalysts.detail: Minutes from the September 15–16 meeting, when the Fed raised rates, are today's clearest scheduled Nasdaq catalyst. Markets have sharply reduced the probability of another October hike after weak payroll growth, so the key question is whether the minutes reinforce a gradual path or reveal broader concern about inflation and the need for additional tightening. A hawkish read would matter most through the long end of the Treasury curve.

catalysts.title: Oil, Gulf of Mexico storm and Saudi-Houthi escalation — ongoing
catalysts.detail: Brent was about $101.65 and WTI $90.38 before the cutoff. A developing Gulf storm threatens facilities responsible for roughly 15% of U.S. crude production and 5% of natural gas output, while escalating Saudi-Houthi tensions add a separate geopolitical risk premium. For Nasdaq, the transmission channel is oil to inflation expectations to long Treasury yields; a sustained move higher in both crude and the 10-year would be the clearest macro threat to today's record-level equity setup.

catalysts.title: AI and semiconductor follow-through — throughout the session
catalysts.detail: Tuesday provided unusually broad fundamental support to the AI infrastructure story: Marvell rose 5.8% after raising its 2028 revenue outlook, AMD gained 2.8% after Lisa Su said supply would be increased substantially in 2027, and Alphabet's 3,590-MW power agreement with Constellation highlighted the scale of data-center electricity demand. The important signal today is whether SOX and secondary semiconductor names continue participating rather than the Nasdaq advance narrowing back toward a few mega-caps.

watchIntoOpen: What I’d watch into the open: the bullish case is that the 10-year settles back from roughly 5.30%, crude's overnight rise remains contained, and SOX continues to confirm the record Nasdaq with broad participation; that would show the AI earnings/capex narrative is still strong enough to absorb macro pressure. The downside case is a simultaneous rise in oil and long yields while semiconductor breadth narrows, which would make the record index level increasingly fragile. I would also watch the market's reaction function around the Fed minutes more than the wording alone: if yields rise on the release but semiconductors hold, that is resilience; if a modestly hawkish interpretation immediately breaks SOX leadership, consolidation risk rises materially.
keyTimes: The U.S. cash market opens at 9:30 ET / 16:30 Istanbul. The major scheduled catalyst is the September FOMC minutes at 2:00 ET / 21:00 Istanbul; Federal Reserve consumer-credit data follow at 3:00 ET / 22:00 Istanbul. Before and after those releases, the most important live variables are the 10-year Treasury yield, crude oil and semiconductor breadth.
